chapter.h1: THE FIRST EPISTLE TO THE CORINTHIANS
chapter.li: LEChapter1 Verse1 Paul, an apostle called of Jesus Christ through the will of God, and Sosthenes our brother, VerseEnd Verse2 unto the church of God which is at Corinth; to them that are sanctified in Christ Jesus, called to be saints with all who in every place call upon the name of Jesus Christ our Lord — both theirs and ours: VerseEnd Verse3 Grace be unto you, and peace from God our Father and from the Lord Jesus Christ. VerseEnd

Verse4 I thank my God always on your behalf for the grace of God which is given you of Jesus Christ, VerseEnd Verse5 that in everything you are enriched of him, in all utterance and in all knowledge, VerseEnd Verse6 even as the testimony of Christ was confirmed in you, VerseEnd Verse7 so that you come behind in no gift, waiting for the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ, VerseEnd Verse8 who shall also confirm you unto the end, that you may be blameless in the day of our Lord Jesus Christ. VerseEnd Verse9 God is faithful, by whom you were called unto the fellowship of his Son Jesus Christ our Lord. VerseEnd

Verse10 Now I implore you, brethren, in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, that you all speak the same thing, and that there be no divisions among you, but that you be perfectly joined together in the same mind and in the same judgment; VerseEnd Verse11 for it has been declared unto me of you, my brethren, by them who are of the house of Chloe, that there are contentions among you. VerseEnd Verse12 Now this I say: that many of you say, I am of Paul, and I of Apollos, and I of Cephas, and I of Christ. VerseEnd Verse13 Is Christ divided? Was Paul crucified for you? Or were you baptized in the name of Paul? VerseEnd Verse14 I thank God that I baptized none of you but Crispus and Gaius, VerseEnd Verse15 lest any should say that I had baptized in my own name. VerseEnd Verse16 And I baptized also the household of Stephanas; besides, I know not whether I baptized any other. VerseEnd

Verse17 For Christ sent me not to baptize, but to preach the gospel — not with wisdom of words, lest the cross of Christ should be made of no effect. VerseEnd Verse18 For the preaching of the cross is to them that perish foolishness, but unto us which are saved, it is the power of God. VerseEnd Verse19 For it is written: I will destroy the wisdom of the wise and will bring to nothing the understanding of the prudent. VerseEnd Verse20 Where is the wise? Where is the scribe? Where is the disputer of this world? Has not God made foolish the wisdom of this world? VerseEnd Verse21 For after that in the wisdom of God the world by wisdom knew not God, it pleased God by the foolishness of preaching to save them that believe. VerseEnd Verse22 For the Jews require a sign, and the Greeks seek after wisdom. VerseEnd Verse23 But we preach Christ crucified, unto the Jews a stumbling block and unto the Greeks foolishness, VerseEnd Verse24 but unto them who believe — both Jews and Greeks — Christ, the power of God and the wisdom of God, VerseEnd Verse25 because the foolishness of God is wiser than men, and the weakness of God is stronger than men. VerseEnd

Verse26 For you see your calling, brethren, that not many wise men after the flesh, not many mighty, not many noble, are chosen. VerseEnd Verse27 For God has chosen the foolish things of the world to confound the wise, and God has chosen the weak things of the world to confound the things which are mighty. VerseEnd Verse28 And base things of the world and things which are despised has God chosen, yea, and things which are not mighty to bring to naught things that are, VerseEnd Verse29 that no flesh should glory in his presence. VerseEnd Verse30 But of him are you in Christ Jesus, who of God is made unto us wisdom, and righteousness, and sanctification, and redemption, VerseEnd Verse31 that according as it is written: He that glories, let him glory in the Lord. VerseEnd

LEChapter2 Verse1 And I, brethren, when I came to you, came not with excellence of speech or of wisdom, declaring unto you the testimony of God. VerseEnd Verse2 For I determined not to know anything among you save Jesus Christ, and him crucified. VerseEnd Verse3 And I was with you in weakness, and in fear, and in much trembling. VerseEnd Verse4 And my speech and my preaching was not with enticing words of man’s wisdom, but in demonstration of the spirit and of power, VerseEnd Verse5 that your faith should not consist in the wisdom of men, but in the power of God. VerseEnd

Verse6 Nevertheless, we speak wisdom among them that are perfect — yet not the wisdom of this world, nor of the princes of this world, that come to naught. VerseEnd Verse7 But we speak the wisdom of God in a mystery, even the hidden wisdom, which God ordained before the world unto our glory, VerseEnd Verse8 which none of the princes of this world knew. For had they known it, they would not have crucified the Lord of glory. VerseEnd

Verse9 But as it is written: Eye has not seen, nor ear heard, neither have entered into the heart of man, the things which God has prepared for them that love him. VerseEnd Verse10 But God has revealed them unto us by his spirit, for the spirit searches all things, yea, the deep things of God. VerseEnd Verse11 For what man knows the things of a man, save the spirit of man which is in him? Even so the things of God knows no man except he has the spirit of God. VerseEnd Verse12 Now we have received not the spirit of the world, but the spirit which is of God, that we might know the things that are freely given to us of God, VerseEnd Verse13 which things also we speak — not in the words which man’s wisdom teaches, but which the holy ghost teaches, comparing spiritual things with spiritual. VerseEnd Verse14 But the natural man receives not the things of the spirit of God, for they are foolishness unto him, neither can he know them, because they are spiritually discerned. VerseEnd Verse15 But he that is spiritual judges all things, yet he himself is judged of no man. VerseEnd Verse16 For who has known the mind of the Lord, that he may instruct him? But we have the mind of Christ. VerseEnd

LEChapter3 Verse1 And I, brethren, could not speak unto you as unto spiritual, but as unto carnal, even as unto babes in Christ. VerseEnd Verse2 I have fed you with milk and not with food, for hitherto you were not able to receive it; neither yet now are you able, VerseEnd Verse3 for you are yet carnal; for whereas there is among you envying, and strife, and divisions, are you not carnal and walk as men? VerseEnd Verse4 For while one says, I am of Paul, and another, I am of Apollos, are you not carnal? VerseEnd

Verse5 Who then is Paul, and who is Apollos, but ministers by whom you believed? Even as the Lord gave to every man? VerseEnd Verse6 I have planted, Apollos watered, but God gave the increase. VerseEnd Verse7 So then neither is he that plants anything, neither he that waters, but God that gives the increase. VerseEnd Verse8 Now he that plants and he that waters are one. And every man shall receive his own reward according to his own labor, VerseEnd Verse9 for we are laborers together with God; you are God’s husbandry, you are God’s building. VerseEnd

Verse10 According to the grace of God which is given unto me, as a wise master builder, I have laid the foundation and another builds thereon. But let every man take heed how he builds thereupon. VerseEnd Verse11 For no other foundation can man lay than that is laid, which is Jesus Christ. VerseEnd Verse12 Now if any man build upon this foundation — gold, silver, precious stones, wood, hay, stubble VerseEnd — Verse13 every man’s work shall be made manifest. For the day shall declare it because it shall be revealed by fire, and the fire shall try every man’s work — of what sort it is. VerseEnd Verse14 If any man’s work abide which he has built thereupon, he shall receive a reward. VerseEnd Verse15 If any man’s work shall be burned, he shall suffer loss. But he himself may be saved, yet so as by fire. VerseEnd

Verse16 Do you not know that you are the temple of God, and that the spirit of God dwells in you? VerseEnd Verse17 If any man defile the temple of God, him shall God destroy. For the temple of God is holy, which temple you are. VerseEnd

Verse18 Let no man deceive himself. If any man among you seems to be wise in this world, let him become a fool, that he may be wise. VerseEnd Verse19 For the wisdom of this world is foolishness with God, for it is written: He takes the wise in their own craftiness. VerseEnd Verse20 And again: The Lord knows the thoughts of the wise, that they are vain. VerseEnd Verse21 Therefore, let no man glory in men; for all things are yours, VerseEnd Verse22 whether Paul, or Apollos, or Cephas, or the world, or life, or death, or things present, or things to come — all are yours, VerseEnd Verse23 and you are Christ’s, and Christ is God’s. VerseEnd

LEChapter4 Verse1 Let a man so account of us as of the ministers of Christ and stewards of the mysteries of God. VerseEnd Verse2 Moreover, it is required of stewards that a man be found faithful. VerseEnd Verse3 But with me it is a very small thing that I should be judged of you or of man’s judgment. Yea, I judge not my own self; VerseEnd Verse4 for though I know nothing against myself, yet I am not hereby justified. But he who judges me is the Lord. VerseEnd Verse5 Therefore, I judge nothing before the time until the Lord come, who both will bring to light the hidden things of darkness and will make manifest the counsels of the hearts. And then shall every man have praise of God. VerseEnd

Verse6 And these things, brethren, I have in a figure transferred to myself and to Apollos for your sakes, that you might learn in us not to think of men above that which is written, that no one of you should be puffed up for one against another. VerseEnd Verse7 For who makes you to differ from another? And what do you have that you did not receive? Now if you did receive it, why do you glory, as if you had not received it? VerseEnd

Verse8 Now you are full. Now you are rich. You have reigned as kings without us, and I would to God you did reign, that we also might reign with you. VerseEnd Verse9 For I think that God has set forth us — the apostles — last, as if appointed to death, for we are made a spectacle unto the world, and to angels, and to men: VerseEnd Verse10 we are fools for Christ’s sake, but you are wise in Christ; we are weak, but you are strong; you are honorable, but we are despised. VerseEnd Verse11 Even unto this present hour we both hunger and thirst, and are naked, and are buffeted, and have no certain dwelling place, VerseEnd Verse12 and labor, working with our own hands. Being reviled, we bless; being persecuted, we suffer it; VerseEnd Verse13 being defamed, we entreat. We are made as the filth of the world, and are the outcasts of all things unto this day. VerseEnd

Verse14 I write not these things to shame you, but as my beloved sons, I warn you. VerseEnd Verse15 For though you have ten thousand instructors in Christ, yet have you not many fathers, for in Christ Jesus I have begotten you through the gospel. VerseEnd Verse16 Wherefore, I implore you, be imitators of me. VerseEnd Verse17 For this cause have I sent unto you Timothy, who is my beloved son and faithful in the Lord, who shall bring you into remembrance of my ways which are in Christ, as I teach everywhere in every church. VerseEnd Verse18 Now some are puffed up, as though I would not come to you. VerseEnd Verse19 But I will come to you shortly, if the Lord desires, and will know not the speech of them who are puffed up, but the power; VerseEnd Verse20 for the kingdom of God is not in word, but in power. VerseEnd Verse21 What do you desire? Shall I come unto you with a rod? Or in love and in the spirit of meekness? VerseEnd

LEChapter5 Verse1 It is reported commonly that there is fornication among you, and such fornication as is not so much as named among the Gentiles: that one should have his father’s wife. VerseEnd Verse2 And you are puffed up and have not rather mourned, that he who has done this deed might be taken away from among you. VerseEnd Verse3 For truly as absent in body, but present in spirit, I have judged already him who has so done this deed, VerseEnd Verse4 as though I were present: in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, when you are gathered together and have the spirit, with the power of our Lord Jesus Christ, VerseEnd Verse5 to deliver such an one unto Satan for the destruction of the flesh, that the spirit may be saved in the day of the Lord Jesus. VerseEnd

Verse6 Your glorying is not good. Do you not know that a little leaven leavens the whole lump? VerseEnd Verse7 Purge out therefore the old leaven, that you may be a new lump, as you are unleavened. For even Christ our passover is sacrificed for us. VerseEnd Verse8 Therefore, let us keep the feast, not with old leaven, neither with the leaven of malice and wickedness, but with the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth. VerseEnd

Verse9 I wrote unto you in an epistle not to company with fornicators, VerseEnd Verse10 yet not altogether with the fornicators of this world, or with the covetous, or extortionists, or with idolaters, for then must you go out of the world. VerseEnd Verse11 But now I have written unto you not to keep company if any man that is called a brother be a fornicator, or covetous, or an idolater, or an abuser, or a drunkard, or an extortionist — with such an one, no, not to eat. VerseEnd Verse12 For what have I to do, to judge them also that are outside? Do not they judge them that are within? VerseEnd Verse13 But them that are outside, God judges; therefore, put away from among yourselves that wicked person. VerseEnd

LEChapter6 Verse1 Do any of you dare, having a matter against another, go to law before the unjust and not before the saints? VerseEnd Verse2 Do you not know that the saints shall judge the world? And if the world shall be judged by you, are you unworthy to judge the smallest matters? VerseEnd Verse3 Do you not know that we shall judge angels? How much more things that pertain to this life? VerseEnd Verse4 If then you have judgments of things pertaining to this life, set them to judge who are least esteemed in the church. VerseEnd Verse5 I speak to your shame. Is it so that there is not a wise man among you? No, not one that shall be able to judge between his brethren? VerseEnd Verse6 But brother goes to law with brother — and that before the unbelievers. VerseEnd

Verse7 Now therefore there is utterly a fault among you because you go to law one with another. Why do you not rather endure wrong? Why do you not rather suffer yourselves to be defrauded? VerseEnd Verse8 Nay, you do wrong and defraud, and that your brethren. VerseEnd Verse9 Do you not know that the unrighteous shall not inherit the kingdom of God? Do not be deceived: neither fornicators, nor idolaters, nor adulterers, nor effeminate, nor abusers of themselves with mankind, VerseEnd Verse10 nor thieves, nor covetous, nor drunkards, nor revilers, nor extortionists shall inherit the kingdom of God. VerseEnd Verse11 And such were some of you. But you are washed, but you are sanctified, but you are justified in the name of the Lord Jesus and by the spirit of our God. VerseEnd Verse12 All these things are not lawful unto me, and all these things are not expedient. All things are not lawful for me; therefore, I will not be brought under the power of any. VerseEnd

Verse13 Food for the belly, and the belly for food, but God shall destroy both it and them. Now the body is not for fornication, but for the Lord, and the Lord for the body. VerseEnd Verse14 And God has both raised up the Lord and will also raise up us by his own power. VerseEnd Verse15 Do you not know that your bodies are the members of Christ? Shall I then take the members of Christ and make them the members of a harlot? God forbid. VerseEnd Verse16 What? Do you not know that he who is joined to a harlot is one body? For two, says he, shall be one flesh. VerseEnd Verse17 But he that is joined unto the Lord is one spirit. VerseEnd Verse18 Flee fornication. Every sin that a man commits is against the body of Christ, and he who commits fornication sins against his own body. VerseEnd Verse19 What? Do you not know that your body is the temple of the holy ghost which is in you, which you have of God? And you are not your own, VerseEnd Verse20 for you are bought with a price. Therefore, glorify God in your body and in your spirit, which are God’s. VerseEnd

LEChapter7 Verse1 Now concerning the things whereof you wrote unto me about, saying it is good for a man not to touch a woman. VerseEnd Verse2 Nevertheless, I say to avoid fornication. Let every man have his own wife, and let every woman have her own husband. VerseEnd Verse3 Let the husband render unto the wife due benevolence, and likewise also the wife unto the husband. VerseEnd Verse4 The wife has not power of her own body, but the husband. And likewise also the husband has not power of his own body, but the wife. VerseEnd Verse5 Depart not one from the other, except it be with consent for a time, that you may give yourselves to fasting and prayer, and come together again, that Satan tempt you not for your lack of self-control. VerseEnd Verse6 And now what I speak is by permission and not by commandment. VerseEnd Verse7 I wish that all men were even as I myself. But every man has his own gift of God, one after this manner and another after that. VerseEnd

Verse8 I say therefore to the unmarried and widows, it is good for them if they abide even as I. VerseEnd Verse9 But if they cannot abide, let them marry, for it is better to marry than that any should commit sin. VerseEnd Verse10 And unto the married I command (yet not I, but the Lord), let not the wife depart from her husband. VerseEnd Verse11 But if she depart, let her remain unmarried or be reconciled to her husband. And let not the husband divorce his wife. VerseEnd

Verse12 But to the rest speak I (not the Lord): If any brother has a wife that believes not, and she be pleased to dwell with him, let him not divorce her. VerseEnd Verse13 And the woman who has a husband that believes not, and if he be pleased to dwell with her, let her not leave him. VerseEnd Verse14 For the unbelieving husband is sanctified by the wife, and the unbelieving wife is sanctified by the husband; else were your children unclean, but now are they holy. VerseEnd Verse15 But if the unbelieving depart, let him depart. A brother or a sister is not under bondage in such cases. But God has called us to peace. VerseEnd Verse16 For do you know, O wife, whether you shall save your husband? Or how do you know, O man, whether you shall save your wife? VerseEnd Verse17 But as God has distributed to every man, as the Lord has called every one, so let him walk, and so ordain I in all churches. VerseEnd

Verse18 Is any man called being circumcised? Let him not become uncircumcised. Is any called in uncircumcision? Let him not be circumcised. VerseEnd Verse19 Circumcision is nothing, and uncircumcision is nothing, but the keeping of the commandments of God. VerseEnd Verse20 Let every man abide in the same calling wherein he was called. VerseEnd Verse21 Are you called, being a servant? Care not for it. But if you may be made free, use it VerseEnd Verse22 rather. For he that is called in the Lord, being a servant, is the Lord’s freeman. Likewise also, he that is called, being free, is Christ’s servant. VerseEnd Verse23 You are bought with a price. Be not the slaves of men. VerseEnd Verse24 Brethren, let every man, wherein he is called, therein abide with God. VerseEnd

Verse25 Now concerning virgins, I have no commandment of the Lord. Yet I give my judgment, as one that has obtained mercy of the Lord, to be faithful. VerseEnd Verse26 I suppose therefore that this is good for the present distress for a man so to remain, that he may do greater good. VerseEnd Verse27 Are you bound unto a wife? Seek not to be released. Are you free from a wife? Seek not a wife. VerseEnd Verse28 But if you marry, you have not sinned. And if a virgin marry, she has not sinned. Nevertheless, such shall have trouble in the flesh. For I spare you not, but I speak unto you who are called unto the ministry. VerseEnd Verse29 For this I say, brethren: the time that remains is but short that you shall be sent forth unto the ministry. Even they who have wives shall be as though they had none, for you are called and chosen to do the Lord’s work. VerseEnd Verse30 And it shall be with those who weep as though they wept not, and those who rejoice as though they rejoiced not, and those who buy as though they possessed not, VerseEnd Verse31 and those who use this world as not using it; for the fashion of this world passes away. VerseEnd Verse32 But I desire, brethren, that you magnify your calling. I would have you without concern. For he who is unmarried cares for the things that belong to the Lord, how he may please the Lord; therefore, he prevails. VerseEnd Verse33 But he who is married cares for the things that are of the world, how he may please his wife; VerseEnd Verse34 therefore, there is a difference, for he is hindered.

There is a difference also between a wife and a virgin. The unmarried woman cares for the things of the Lord, that she may be holy both in body and in spirit. But she that is married cares for the things of the world, how she may please her husband. VerseEnd Verse35 And this I speak for your own profit, not that I may cast a snare upon you, but for that which is comely, and that you may attend upon the Lord without distraction. VerseEnd Verse36 But if any man thinks that he behaves himself uncomely toward his virgin whom he has betrothed, if she pass the flower of age and need so require, let him do what he has promised, he sins not. Let them marry. VerseEnd Verse37 Nevertheless, he that stands steadfast in his heart, having no necessity, but has power over his own will and has so decreed in his heart that he will keep his virgin does well. VerseEnd Verse38 So then he that gives himself in marriage does well, but he that gives himself not in marriage does better. VerseEnd

Verse39 The wife is bound by the law as long as her husband lives. But if her husband is dead, she is at liberty to be married to whom she desires, only in the Lord. VerseEnd Verse40 But she is happier if she so abide (after my judgment, and I think also that I have the spirit of God) VerseEnd.

LEChapter8 Verse1 Now as touching things offered unto idols, we know that we all have knowledge. Knowledge puffs up, but charity edifies. VerseEnd Verse2 And if any man thinks that he knows anything, he knows nothing yet as he ought to know. VerseEnd Verse3 But if any man loves God, the same is known of him. VerseEnd

Verse4 As concerning therefore the eating of those things which are in the world offered in sacrifice unto idols, we know that an idol is nothing, and that there is no other God but one. VerseEnd Verse5 For though there be that are called gods, whether in Heaven or in earth (as there are gods many and lords many) VerseEnd, Verse6 but to us there is but one God — the Father — of whom are all things (and we in him), and one Lord Jesus Christ, by whom are all things (and we by him) VerseEnd.

Verse7 Nevertheless, there is not in every man that knowledge. For some with conscience of the idol unto this hour eat it as a thing offered unto an idol, and their conscience being weak is defiled. VerseEnd Verse8 But food commends us not to God; for neither if we eat are we the better, neither if we eat not are we the worse. VerseEnd Verse9 But take heed, lest by any means this liberty of yours become a stumbling block to them that are weak. VerseEnd Verse10 For if any man sees you, who has knowledge, sit at a meal in the idol’s temple, shall not the conscience of him who is weak be emboldened to eat those things which are offered to idols? VerseEnd Verse11 And through your knowledge shall the weak brother perish, for whom Christ died. VerseEnd Verse12 When you sin so against the brethren and wound their weak conscience, you sin against Christ. VerseEnd Verse13 Wherefore, if food make my brother to offend, I will eat no flesh while the world stands, lest I make my brother to offend. VerseEnd

LEChapter9 Verse1 Am I not an apostle? Am I not free? Have I not seen Jesus Christ our Lord? Are you not my work in the Lord? VerseEnd Verse2 If I am not an apostle unto others, yet doubtless I am to you, for the seal of my apostleship are you in the Lord. VerseEnd

Verse3 My answer to them that do examine me is this: VerseEnd Verse4 Do we not have power to eat and to drink? VerseEnd Verse5 Do we not have power to lead about a sister, a wife, as well as other apostles, and as the brethren of the Lord, and Cephas? VerseEnd Verse6 Or I only, and Barnabas, do we not have power to cease working? VerseEnd Verse7 Who serves as a soldier any time at his own expense? Who plants a vineyard and eats not of the fruit thereof? Or who feeds a flock and eats not of the milk of the flock? VerseEnd Verse8 Do I say these things as a man? Or does not the law say the same also? VerseEnd Verse9 For it is written in the law of Moses: You shall not muzzle the mouth of the ox that treads out the grain. Does God take care for oxen? VerseEnd Verse10 Or does he say it altogether for our sakes? For our sakes no doubt this is written, that he who plows should plow in hope and that he who threshes in hope should be partaker of his hope. VerseEnd

Verse11 If we have sown unto you spiritual things, is it a great thing if we shall reap your carnal things? VerseEnd Verse12 If others are partakers of this power over you, are not we rather? Nevertheless, we have not used this power, but suffer all things, lest we should hinder the gospel of Christ. VerseEnd Verse13 Do you not know that they who minister about holy things live of the things of the temple? And they who wait at the altar are partakers with the altar? VerseEnd Verse14 Even so has the Lord ordained that they who preach the gospel should live of the gospel. VerseEnd Verse15 But I have used none of these things, neither have I written these things that it should be so done unto me. For it would be better for me to die than that any man should make my glorying void. VerseEnd Verse16 For though I preach the gospel, I have nothing to glory of, for necessity is laid upon me. Yea, woe is unto me if I preach not the gospel; VerseEnd Verse17 for if I do this thing willingly, I have a reward, but if against my will (a dispensation of the gospel is committed unto me) VerseEnd, Verse18 what is my reward then? Truly that when I preach the gospel, I may make the gospel of Christ without charge, that I abuse not my power in the gospel. VerseEnd

Verse19 For though I am free from all men, yet have I made myself servant unto all, that I might gain the more. VerseEnd Verse20 And unto the Jews I became as a Jew, that I might gain the Jews. To them who are under the law, as under the law, that I might gain them who are under the law. VerseEnd Verse21 To them who are without law, as without law — being not without law to God, but under the law to Christ — that I might gain them who are without law. VerseEnd Verse22 To the weak became I as weak, that I might gain the weak. I am made all things to all men, that I might by all means save some. VerseEnd Verse23 And this I do for the gospel’s sake, that I might be partaker thereof with you. VerseEnd

Verse24 Do you not know that they who run in a race all run, but only one receives the prize? So run, that you may obtain. VerseEnd Verse25 And every man that strives for the mastery is temperate in all things. Now they do it to obtain a corruptible crown, but we an incorruptible. VerseEnd Verse26 I therefore so run, not as uncertainly; so fight I, not as one that beats the air. VerseEnd Verse27 But I keep my body under and bring it into subjection, lest by any means, when I have preached to others, I myself should be a castaway. VerseEnd

LEChapter10 Verse1 Moreover brethren, I desire not that you should be ignorant that all our fathers were under the cloud, and all passed through the sea, VerseEnd Verse2 and were all baptized unto Moses in the cloud and in the sea, VerseEnd Verse3 and did all eat the same spiritual food, VerseEnd Verse4 and did all drink the same spiritual drink, for they drank of that spiritual Rock that followed them, and that Rock was Christ. VerseEnd Verse5 But with many of them God was not well pleased, for they were overthrown in the wilderness. VerseEnd

Verse6 Now these things were our examples, to the intent we should not lust after evil things as they also lusted, VerseEnd Verse7 neither be idolaters as were some of them, as it is written: The people sat down to eat and drink, and rose up to play. VerseEnd Verse8 Neither let us commit fornication as some of them committed, and fell in one day twenty-three thousand. VerseEnd Verse9 Neither let us test Christ as some of them also tested and were destroyed of serpents. VerseEnd Verse10 Neither murmur as some of them also murmured and were destroyed of the destroyer. VerseEnd Verse11 Now all these things happened unto them for examples, and they are written for our admonition also, and for an admonition for those upon whom the end of the world shall come. VerseEnd Verse12 Wherefore, let him that thinks he stands take heed, lest he fall. VerseEnd Verse13 There has no temptation taken you but such as is common to man. But God is faithful, who will not suffer you to be tempted above that you are able, but will with the temptation also make a way to escape, that you may be able to bear it. VerseEnd Verse14 Wherefore, my dearly beloved, flee from idolatry. VerseEnd Verse15 I speak as to wise men. Judge what I say. VerseEnd

Verse16 The cup of blessing which we bless, is it not the communion of the blood of Christ? The bread which we break, is it not the communion of the body of Christ? VerseEnd Verse17 For we being many are one bread and one body, for we are all partakers of that one bread. VerseEnd Verse18 Behold Israel after the flesh: are not they who eat of the sacrifices partakers of the altar? VerseEnd Verse19 What do I say then? That the idol is anything? Or that which is offered in sacrifice to idols is anything? VerseEnd Verse20 But I say that the things which the Gentiles sacrifice, they sacrifice to devils and not to God. And I desire not that you should have fellowship with devils. VerseEnd Verse21 You cannot drink the cup of the Lord and the cup of devils. You cannot be partakers of the Lord’s table and of the table of devils. VerseEnd

Verse22 Do we provoke the Lord to jealousy? Are we stronger than he? VerseEnd Verse23 All things are not lawful for me, for all things are not expedient. All things are not lawful, for all things edify not. VerseEnd Verse24 Let no man seek therefore his own, but every man another’s good. VerseEnd Verse25 Whatever is sold in the butcher’s stall, that eat, asking no question for conscience sake. VerseEnd Verse26 For the earth is the Lord’s, and the fullness thereof. VerseEnd Verse27 If any of them that believe not bid you eat, and you be disposed to go, whatever is set before you, eat, asking no question for conscience sake. VerseEnd Verse28 But if any man say unto you, This is offered in sacrifice unto idols, eat not for his sake that showed it, and for conscience sake. For the earth is the Lord’s, and the fullness thereof — conscience, VerseEnd Verse29 I say, not your own, but of the other. For why is my liberty judged of another man’s conscience? VerseEnd Verse30 For if I by grace be a partaker, why am I evil spoken of for that for which I give thanks? VerseEnd

Verse31 Whether therefore you eat, or drink, or whatever you do, do all to the glory of God. VerseEnd Verse32 Give no offense, neither to the Jews, nor to the Gentiles, nor to the church of God, VerseEnd Verse33 even as I please all men in all things, not seeking my own profit, but of the many, that they may be saved. VerseEnd LEChapter11 Verse1 Be imitators of me, even as I also am of Christ. VerseEnd

Verse2 Now I praise you, brethren, that you remember me in all things, and keep the ordinances as I delivered them to you. VerseEnd Verse3 But I would have you know that the head of every man is Christ, and the head of the woman is the man, and the head of Christ is God. VerseEnd Verse4 Every man praying or prophesying having his head covered dishonors his head. VerseEnd Verse5 But every woman that prays or prophesies with her head uncovered dishonors her head, for that is even all one, as if she were shaven. VerseEnd Verse6 For if the woman be not covered, let her also be shorn. But if it be a shame for a woman to be shorn or shaven, let her be covered. VerseEnd Verse7 For a man indeed ought not to cover his head, forasmuch as he is the image and glory of God. But the woman is the glory of the man, VerseEnd Verse8 for the man is not of the woman but the woman of the man, VerseEnd Verse9 neither was the man created for the woman but the woman for the man. VerseEnd Verse10 For this cause ought the woman to have a covering on her head: because of the angels. VerseEnd Verse11 Nevertheless, neither is the man without the woman, neither the woman without the man, in the Lord. VerseEnd Verse12 For as the woman is of the man, even so is the man also by the woman; but all things of God. VerseEnd Verse13 Judge in yourselves: Is it comely that a woman pray unto God uncovered? VerseEnd Verse14 Does not even nature itself teach you that if a man have long hair, it is a shame unto him? VerseEnd Verse15 But if a woman have long hair, it is a glory to her, for her hair is given her for a covering. VerseEnd Verse16 But if any man seem to be contentious, we have no such custom, neither the churches of God. VerseEnd

Verse17 Now in this that I declare unto you, I praise you not that you come together not for the better, but for the worse. VerseEnd Verse18 For first of all, when you come together in the church, I hear that there are divisions among you and I partly believe it, VerseEnd Verse19 for there must be also divisions among you, that they who are approved may be made manifest among you. VerseEnd Verse20 When you come together into one place, is it not to eat the Lord’s supper? VerseEnd Verse21 But in eating, everyone takes before another his own supper, and one is hungry, and another is drunk. VerseEnd Verse22 What? Do you not have houses to eat and to drink in? Or do you despise the church of God and shame them that have not? What shall I say to you? Shall I praise you in this? I praise you not. VerseEnd

Verse23 For I have received of the Lord that which also I delivered unto you — that the Lord Jesus, the same night in which he was betrayed, took bread. VerseEnd Verse24 And when he had given thanks, he broke it, and said, Take, eat; this is my body, which is broken for you. This do in remembrance of me. VerseEnd Verse25 After the same manner also he took the cup, when he had supped, saying, This cup is the new covenant in my blood. This do, as oft as you drink it, in remembrance of me. VerseEnd Verse26 For as often as you eat this bread and drink this cup, you do show the Lord’s death until he come. VerseEnd Verse27 Wherefore, whoever shall eat this bread and drink this cup of the Lord unworthily shall be guilty of the body and blood of the Lord. VerseEnd Verse28 But let a man examine himself, and so let him eat of that bread and drink of that cup. VerseEnd Verse29 For he that eats and drinks unworthily eats and drinks condemnation to himself, not discerning the Lord’s body. VerseEnd Verse30 For this cause, many are weak and sickly among you, and many sleep. VerseEnd Verse31 For if we would judge ourselves, we should not be judged. VerseEnd Verse32 But when we are judged, we are chastened of the Lord, that we should not be condemned with the world. VerseEnd Verse33 Wherefore, my brethren, when you come together to eat, wait one for another. VerseEnd Verse34 And if any man hunger, let him eat at home, that you come not together unto condemnation. And the rest will I set in order when I come. VerseEnd

LEChapter12 Verse1 Now concerning spiritual things, brethren, I would not have you ignorant. VerseEnd Verse2 You know that you were Gentiles, carried away unto these dumb idols even as you were led. VerseEnd Verse3 Wherefore, I give you to understand that no man speaking by the spirit of God calls Jesus accursed, and that no man can know that Jesus is the Lord but by the holy ghost. VerseEnd

Verse4 Now there are diversities of gifts, but the same spirit. VerseEnd Verse5 And there are differences of administrations, but the same Lord. VerseEnd Verse6 And there are diversities of operations, but it is the same God who works all in all. VerseEnd Verse7 But the manifestation of the spirit is given to every man to profit all; VerseEnd Verse8 for to one is given by the spirit the word of wisdom, to another the word of knowledge by the same spirit, VerseEnd Verse9 to another faith by the same spirit, to another the gifts of healing by the same spirit, VerseEnd Verse10 to another the working of miracles, to another prophecy, to another discerning of spirits, to another kinds of tongues, to another the interpretation of tongues. VerseEnd Verse11 But all these work that one and the selfsame spirit, dividing to every man separately as he desires. VerseEnd

Verse12 For as the body is one and has many members, and all the members of that one body, being many, are one body, so also is Christ. VerseEnd Verse13 For by one spirit are we all baptized into one body, whether we are Jews or Gentiles, whether we are bond or free, and have been all made to drink into one spirit. VerseEnd Verse14 For the body is not one member, but many. VerseEnd Verse15 If the foot shall say, Because I am not the hand, I am not of the body — is it therefore not of the body? VerseEnd Verse16 And if the ear shall say, Because I am not the eye, I am not of the body — is it therefore not of the body? VerseEnd Verse17 If the whole body were an eye, where would be the hearing? If the whole were hearing, where would be the smelling? VerseEnd Verse18 But now has God set the members, every one of them, in the body as it has pleased him. VerseEnd Verse19 And if they were all one member, where would be the body? VerseEnd Verse20 But now are they many members, yet but one body. VerseEnd Verse21 And the eye cannot say unto the hand, I have no need of you. Nor again the head to the feet, I have no need of you. VerseEnd Verse22 Nay, much more those members of the body which seem to be more feeble are necessary, VerseEnd Verse23 and those members of the body which we think to be less honorable, upon these we bestow more abundant honor. And our uncomely parts have more abundant comeliness, VerseEnd Verse24 for our comely parts have no need. But God has tempered the body together, having given more abundant honor to that part which lacked, VerseEnd Verse25 that there should be no schism in the body, but that the members should have the same care one for another. VerseEnd Verse26 And whether one member suffer, all the members suffer with it; or one member is honored, all the members rejoice with it. VerseEnd Verse27 Now you are the body of Christ, and members in particular. VerseEnd

Verse28 And God has set some in the church: first apostles, secondarily prophets, thirdly teachers; after that, miracles, then gifts of healings, helps, governments, diversities of tongues. VerseEnd Verse29 Are all apostles? Are all prophets? Are all teachers? Are all workers of miracles? VerseEnd Verse30 Do all have the gifts of healing? Do all speak with tongues? Do all interpret? VerseEnd Verse31 I say unto you, nay, for I have shown unto you a more excellent way. Therefore, covet earnestly the best gifts. VerseEnd

LEChapter13 Verse1 Though I speak with the tongues of men and of angels, and have not charity, I have become as sounding brass or a tinkling cymbal. VerseEnd Verse2 And though I have the gift of prophecy and understand all mysteries and all knowledge, and though I have all faith so that I could remove mountains, and have not charity, I am nothing. VerseEnd Verse3 And though I bestow all my goods to feed the poor, and though I give my body to be burned, and have not charity, it profits me nothing. VerseEnd

Verse4 Charity suffers long and is kind. Charity envies not. Charity vaunts not itself, is not puffed up, VerseEnd Verse5 does not behave itself unseemly, seeks not her own, is not easily provoked, thinks no evil, VerseEnd Verse6 rejoices not in iniquity but rejoices in the truth, VerseEnd Verse7 bears all things, believes all things, hopes all things, endures all things. VerseEnd

Verse8 Charity never fails. But whether there are prophecies, they shall fail; whether there are tongues, they shall cease; whether there is knowledge, it shall vanish away. VerseEnd Verse9 For we know in part and we prophesy in part, VerseEnd Verse10 but when that which is perfect has come, then that which is in part shall be done away. VerseEnd Verse11 When I was a child, I spoke as a child, I understood as a child, I thought as a child; but when I became a man, I put away childish things. VerseEnd Verse12 For now we see through a mirror, darkly, but then face to face. Now I know in part, but then shall I know even as also I am known. VerseEnd Verse13 And now abide faith, hope, charity — these three; but the greatest of these is charity. VerseEnd

LEChapter14 Verse1 Follow after charity and desire spiritual gifts, but rather that you may prophesy. VerseEnd Verse2 For he that speaks in another tongue speaks not unto men but unto God, for no man understands him; nevertheless, in the spirit he speaks mysteries. VerseEnd Verse3 But he that prophesies speaks unto men to edification, and exhortation, and comfort. VerseEnd Verse4 He that speaks in another tongue edifies himself, but he that prophesies edifies the church. VerseEnd Verse5 I wish that you all spoke with tongues, but rather that you prophesied, for greater is he that prophesies than he that speaks with tongues — except he interpret, that the church may receive edifying. VerseEnd

Verse6 Now brethren, if I come unto you speaking with tongues, what shall I profit you except I shall speak to you either by revelation, or by knowledge, or by prophesying, or by doctrine? VerseEnd Verse7 And even things without life giving sound, whether pipe or harp, except they give a distinction in the sounds, how shall it be known what is piped or harped? VerseEnd Verse8 For if the trumpet give an uncertain sound, who shall prepare himself to the battle? VerseEnd Verse9 So likewise you, except you utter by the tongue words easy to be understood, how shall it be known what is spoken? For you shall speak into the air. VerseEnd Verse10 There are, it may be, so many kinds of voices in the world, and none of them is without signification. VerseEnd Verse11 Therefore, if I know not the meaning of the voice, I shall be unto him that speaks a foreigner, and he that speaks shall be a foreigner unto me. VerseEnd Verse12 Even so you, forasmuch as you are zealous of spiritual gifts, seek that you may excel to the edifying of the church. VerseEnd Verse13 Wherefore, let him that speaks in another tongue pray that he may interpret. VerseEnd Verse14 For if I pray in another tongue, my spirit prays, but my understanding is unfruitful. VerseEnd

Verse15 What is it then? I will pray with the spirit, and I will pray with the understanding also. I will sing with the spirit, and I will sing with the understanding also. VerseEnd Verse16 Else when you shall bless with the spirit, how shall he that occupies the place of the unlearned say, Amen, at your giving of thanks, seeing he understands not what you say? VerseEnd Verse17 For you truly give thanks well, but the other is not edified. VerseEnd Verse18 I thank my God I speak with tongues more than you all, VerseEnd Verse19 yet in the church I would rather speak five words with my understanding, that by my voice I might teach others also, than ten thousand words in another tongue. VerseEnd

Verse20 Brethren, be not children in understanding. Nevertheless, in malice be children, but in understanding be men. VerseEnd Verse21 In the law it is written: With men of other tongues and other lips will I speak unto this people, and yet for all that will they not hear me, says the Lord. VerseEnd Verse22 Wherefore, tongues are for a sign not to them who believe, but to them who believe not; but prophesying serves not for them who believe not, but for them who believe. VerseEnd Verse23 If therefore the whole church has come together into one place and all speak with tongues, and there come in those who are unlearned or unbelievers, will they not say that you are mad? VerseEnd Verse24 But if all prophesy, and there come in one that believes not, or one unlearned, he is convicted of all, he is judged of all, VerseEnd Verse25 and thus are the secrets of his heart made manifest. And so falling down on his face, he will worship God and report that God is in you truly. VerseEnd

Verse26 How is it then, brethren? When you come together, every one of you has a psalm, has a doctrine, has a tongue, has a revelation, has an interpretation. Let all things be done unto edifying. VerseEnd Verse27 If any man speak in another tongue, let it be by two or at the most by three, and that by course; and let one interpret. VerseEnd Verse28 But if there be no interpreter, let him keep silence in the church, and let him speak to himself and to God. VerseEnd Verse29 Let the prophets speak, two or three, and let the other judge. VerseEnd Verse30 If anything be revealed to another that sits by, let the first hold his peace. VerseEnd Verse31 For you may all prophesy one by one, that all may learn and all may be comforted. VerseEnd Verse32 And the spirits of the prophets are subject to the prophets. VerseEnd Verse33 For God is not the author of confusion, but of peace, as in all churches of the saints. VerseEnd

Verse34 Let your women keep silence in the churches, for it is not permitted unto them to rule, but they are commanded to be under obedience, as also says the law. VerseEnd Verse35 And if they will learn anything, let them ask their husbands at home, for it is a shame for women to rule in the church. VerseEnd

Verse36 What? Did the word of God come out from you? Or did it come unto you only? VerseEnd Verse37 If any man think himself to be a prophet or spiritual, let him acknowledge that the things that I write unto you are the commandments of the Lord. VerseEnd Verse38 But if any man be ignorant, let him be ignorant. VerseEnd Verse39 Wherefore, brethren, covet to prophesy, and forbid not to speak with tongues. VerseEnd Verse40 Let all things be done decently and in order. VerseEnd

LEChapter15 Verse1 Moreover brethren, I declare unto you the gospel which I preached unto you, which also you have received and wherein you stand, VerseEnd Verse2 by which also you are saved if you keep in memory what I preached unto you, unless you have believed in vain. VerseEnd Verse3 For I delivered unto you first of all that which I also received: that Christ died for our sins according to the scriptures, VerseEnd Verse4 and that he was buried, and that he rose again the third day according to the scriptures, VerseEnd Verse5 and that he was seen of Cephas, then of the twelve. VerseEnd Verse6 After that, he was seen of above five hundred brethren at once, of whom the greater part remain unto this present, but some are fallen asleep. VerseEnd Verse7 After that, he was seen of James, then of all the apostles. VerseEnd Verse8 And last of all, he was seen of me also, as of one born out of due time. VerseEnd Verse9 For I am the least of the apostles, that am not meet to be called an apostle because I persecuted the church of God. VerseEnd Verse10 But by the grace of God, I am what I am. And his grace which was bestowed upon me was not in vain, for I labored more abundantly than they all — yet not I, but the grace of God which was with me. VerseEnd Verse11 Therefore, whether it were I or they, so we preach, and so you believed. VerseEnd

Verse12 Now if Christ be preached, that he rose from the dead, how say some among you that there is no resurrection of the dead? VerseEnd Verse13 But if there be no resurrection of the dead, then is Christ not risen. VerseEnd Verse14 And if Christ is not risen, then is our preaching vain and your faith is also vain. VerseEnd Verse15 Yea, and we are found false witnesses of God because we have testified of God that he raised up Christ, whom he raised not up if it so be that the dead rise not. VerseEnd Verse16 For if the dead rise not, then is not Christ raised; VerseEnd Verse17 and if Christ is not raised, your faith is vain, you are yet in your sins. VerseEnd Verse18 Then they also who are fallen asleep in Christ are perished. VerseEnd Verse19 If in this life only we have hope in Christ, we are of all men most miserable. VerseEnd

Verse20 But now has Christ risen from the dead and become the firstfruits of them that slept. VerseEnd Verse21 For since by man came death, by man came also the resurrection of the dead. VerseEnd Verse22 For as in Adam all die, even so in Christ shall all be made alive; VerseEnd Verse23 but every man in his own order: Christ, the firstfruits; afterward, they that are Christ’s at his coming; VerseEnd Verse24 afterward comes the end, when he shall have delivered up the kingdom to God, even the Father, when he shall have put down all rule and all authority and power, VerseEnd Verse25 for he must reign until he has put all enemies under his feet. VerseEnd Verse26 The last enemy, death, shall be destroyed. VerseEnd Verse27 For he says, when it is manifest that he has put all things under his feet, and that all things are put under, he is excepted of the Father, who did put all things under him. VerseEnd Verse28 And when all things shall be subdued unto him, then shall the Son also himself be subject unto him that put all things under him, that God may be all in all. VerseEnd

Verse29 Else what shall they do who are baptized for the dead, if the dead rise not at all? Why are they then baptized for the dead? VerseEnd Verse30 And why do we stand in jeopardy every hour? VerseEnd Verse31 I protest unto you the resurrection of the dead, and this is my rejoicing which I have in Christ Jesus our Lord daily, though I die. VerseEnd Verse32 If after the manner of men I have fought with beasts at Ephesus, what does it advantage me if the dead rise not? Let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we die. VerseEnd Verse33 Be not deceived. Evil communications corrupt good manners. VerseEnd Verse34 Awake to righteousness and sin not, for some have not the knowledge of God. I speak this to your shame. VerseEnd

Verse35 But some man will say, How are the dead raised up? And with what body do they VerseEnd Verse36 come? You fool, that which you sow is not quickened except it die. VerseEnd Verse37 And that which you sow, you sow not that body which shall be, but grain — it may be of wheat, or some other. VerseEnd Verse38 But God gives it a body as it has pleased him, and to every seed his own body. VerseEnd Verse39 All flesh is not the same flesh, but there is one kind of flesh of men, another flesh of beasts, another of fish, and another of birds. VerseEnd Verse40 Also celestial bodies, and bodies terrestrial, and bodies telestial; but the glory of the celestial, one, and the terrestrial, another, and the telestial, another. VerseEnd Verse41 There is one glory of the sun, and another glory of the moon, and another glory of the stars, for one star differs from another star in glory. VerseEnd

Verse42 So also is the resurrection of the dead: it is sown in corruption, it is raised in incorruption; VerseEnd Verse43 it is sown in dishonor, it is raised in glory; it is sown in weakness, it is raised in power; VerseEnd Verse44 it is sown a natural body, it is raised a spiritual body. There is a natural body, and there is a spiritual body. VerseEnd Verse45 And so it is written: The first man Adam was made a living soul, the last Adam was made a quickening spirit. VerseEnd Verse46 Nevertheless, that which is natural first, and not that which is spiritual, but afterward that which is spiritual VerseEnd — Verse47 the first is man of the earth: earthy; the second man is the Lord from Heaven. VerseEnd Verse48 As is the earthy, such are they also that are earthy. And as is the Heavenly, such are they also that are Heavenly. VerseEnd Verse49 And as we have borne the image of the earthy, we shall also bear the image of the Heavenly. VerseEnd

Verse50 Now this I say, brethren, that flesh and blood cannot inherit the kingdom of God. Neither does corruption inherit incorruption. VerseEnd Verse51 Behold, I show you a mystery: we shall not all sleep, but we shall all be changed VerseEnd Verse52 in a moment, in the twinkling of an eye, at the sound of the trump. For the trumpet shall sound, and the dead shall be raised incorruptible, and we shall be changed. VerseEnd Verse53 For this corruptible must put on incorruption, and this mortal must put on immortality. VerseEnd Verse54 So when this corruptible shall have put on incorruption, and this mortal shall have put on immortality, then shall be brought to pass the saying that is written: Death is swallowed up in victory. VerseEnd Verse55 O death, where is your sting? O grave, where is your victory? VerseEnd Verse56 The sting of death is sin; and the strength of sin is the law. VerseEnd Verse57 But thanks be to God, who gives us the victory through our Lord Jesus Christ. VerseEnd
Verse58 Therefore, my beloved brethren, be steadfast, immovable, always abounding in the work of the Lord, forasmuch as you know that your labor is not in vain in the Lord. VerseEnd

LEChapter16 Verse1 Now concerning the collection for the saints, as I have given order to the churches of Galatia, even so do you. VerseEnd Verse2 Upon the first day of the week, let every one of you lay by him in store as God has prospered him, that there be no gatherings when I come. VerseEnd Verse3 And when I come, whomever you shall approve by your letters, them will I send to bring your liberality unto Jerusalem. VerseEnd Verse4 And if it be meet that I go also, they shall go with me. VerseEnd

Verse5 Now I will come unto you when I shall pass through Macedonia, for I do pass through Macedonia. VerseEnd Verse6 And it may be that I will stay, yea, and winter with you, that you may bring me on my journey wherever I go. VerseEnd Verse7 For I will not see you now by the way, but I trust to linger a while with you, if the Lord permit. VerseEnd Verse8 But I will remain at Ephesus until Pentecost. VerseEnd Verse9 For a great door, and effectual, is opened unto me, but there are many adversaries. VerseEnd

Verse10 Now if Timothy come, see that he may be with you without fear, for he works the work of the Lord, as I also do. VerseEnd Verse11 Let no man therefore despise him, but conduct him forth in peace, that he may come unto me, for I look for him with the brethren. VerseEnd

Verse12 As touching our brother Apollos, I greatly desired him to come unto you with the brethren, but his will was not at all to come at this time. But he will come when he shall have convenient time. VerseEnd

Verse13 Watch, stand fast in the faith, conduct yourselves like men, be strong. VerseEnd Verse14 Let all your things be done with charity. VerseEnd Verse15 I implore you, brethren (you know the house of Stephanas, that it is the firstfruits of Achaia, and that they have devoted themselves to the ministry of the saints) VerseEnd, Verse16 that you submit yourselves unto such, and to everyone that helps with us and labors. VerseEnd Verse17 I am glad of the coming of Stephanas, and Fortunatus, and Achaicus, for that which was lacking on your part, they have supplied; VerseEnd Verse18 for they have refreshed my spirit and yours. Therefore, acknowledge them that are such. VerseEnd

Verse19 The churches of Asia salute you. Aquila and Priscilla salute you much in the Lord, with the church that is in their house. VerseEnd Verse20 All the brethren greet you. Greet one another with a holy salutation, VerseEnd Verse21 the salutation of me, Paul, with my own hand. VerseEnd

Verse22 If any man love not the Lord Jesus Christ, let him be anathema. Our Lord has come. VerseEnd Verse23 The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you. VerseEnd Verse24 My love be with you all in Christ Jesus. Amen. VerseEnd

p.i: The first epistle to the Corinthians was written from Philippi by Stephanas, and Fortunatus, and Achaicus, and Timothy.
